title: Security event: Prompt leakage for requests in June and July of 2026
gist: Together AI disclosed that an unauthorized party downloaded stored customer prompt samples (from MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 requests in June-July 2026) after an AI coding agent committed a Hugging Face credential to Together's public GitHub repo xorl. The attacker mined the prompts for further credentials; Together responded with scoped/short-lived credentials, PR secret scanning, default zero data retention for new accounts, and new rules for AI coding agents.

insights.claim: Together AI's serverless inference prompt leak originated when an AI coding agent committed a credential for a private Hugging Face repository into Together's public GitHub repository xorl.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: A concrete, CEO-acknowledged case of an AI coding agent causing a customer-data breach — supports demand for secret-scanning and agent-governance tooling and raises operational-risk scrutiny of agentic dev workflows.
insights.quote: an AI coding agent committed a credential that provided access to the private Hugging Face repository

insights.claim: Together AI's automated scanning detected the exposed credential and the commit was reverted, but an unauthorized party still obtained and used the credential during the exposure window — detection-and-revert did not prevent exploitation.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Reverting a leaked secret is insufficient once public; watch for shift toward pre-commit blocking and short-lived/keyless credentials as the standard control.
insights.quote: Our automated scanning detected the exposed credential, and we reverted the commit.
insights.locator: During development of our public GitHub repository

insights.claim: Customer prompt samples used for Together AI's routine software testing were stored in a private Hugging Face repository, drawn from requests to MiniMax M3, GLM-5.2 and Kimi K2.6 primarily on June 24, July 4, July 8 and July 14, 2026.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Inference providers retaining customer prompts for internal testing creates latent data-exposure risk; customers of open-model hosts should audit retention practices.
insights.locator: As part of routine software testing

themes.theme: Attacker behavior: prompts as credential mine

insights.claim: The attacker who downloaded Together AI's stored prompt samples searched them for credentials to other services and tested whether those credentials were valid, showing LLM prompts frequently contain reusable secrets.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Prompt logs are a high-value secondary-credential target; a leak at one inference provider can cascade into downstream customer systems.
insights.quote: The party subsequently searched those samples for credentials to other services and tested whether those credentials were valid.

insights.claim: Five of the credentials the attacker tested after the Together AI prompt leak were canary credentials tied to a Dragos security experiment, which helped surface the malicious use.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Canary/honeytoken credentials planted in prompts act as tripwires for downstream abuse — a validating use case for deception-based security tooling.
insights.quote: Five of the credentials tested were canary credentials associated with a Dragos security experiment.

insights.claim: Together AI engaged an external forensic investigation firm and law enforcement and says it has found no evidence of prompt leakage beyond this incident, though review of whether sensitive personal or customer data was exposed is still ongoing.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Scope is not final — follow-up customer notifications could widen reputational and contractual exposure for Together AI.
insights.quote: we have not identified evidence of additional prompt leakage beyond this incident

themes.theme: Remediation: ZDR default and agent controls

insights.claim: After the prompt leak, Together AI made zero data retention (ZDR) the default setting for new accounts and advised customers handling sensitive prompt data to enable ZDR.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Default-ZDR may become a competitive baseline for inference providers, limiting their ability to use customer prompts for testing or model improvement.
insights.quote: Making zero data retention (ZDR) the default setting for new accounts.

insights.claim: Together AI responded to the credential exposure by adopting scoped or short-lived credentials and keyless access where supported, checking all pull requests for credentials, and updating its development processes governing AI coding agents.
insights.speaker: Vipul Ved Prakash
insights.so_what: Playbook for agentic-dev security (ephemeral creds, PR secret scanning, agent usage policy) — a demand signal for secrets-management and workload-identity vendors.
insights.quote: Updating our development processes governing the use of AI coding agents.
